title: Static electricity
examples: How does rubbing things together create electricity?
What is the difference between charging by friction and induction?
Can static electricity make things jump?

explain.say: When you rub certain materials together you can build up a charge.
For example rubbing a balloon on your hair moves electrons from your hair to the balloon.
Induction means bringing a charged object near a neutral object without touching it.
If you bring a negatively charged rod near a neutral ball it will cause the ball to become charged.
A spark happens when the accumulated charge is strong enough to jump to another object.
In real life when you pull a clothes from a dry machine you might see a small spark.

items: A spark can occur when the charge is high

faq.q: Why does rubbing a balloon make it stick to the wall?
faq.a: Rubbing the balloon transfers electrons, giving it a charge. This charged balloon is then attracted to the wall, which has a charge difference.
asks: How does static electricity make things stick?
What is happening when the balloon sticks?

faq.q: Is induction the same as friction?
faq.a: No, friction involves physical rubbing to transfer charge. Induction involves using a nearby charged object to force a charge onto a neutral object without touching it.
asks: Do I have to touch the object for induction?
What is the difference between the two charging methods?

faq.q: What causes a spark to jump?
faq.a: A spark happens when the electric potential difference, or voltage, becomes very high. The charge jumps across the air gap to reach a lower potential.

faq.q: Can I charge things just by bringing them close?
faq.a: Yes, that is called induction. You can use a charged object to influence a neutral object nearby without any direct contact.
asks: Is proximity enough to charge something?
What is the process of charging nearby?

faq.q: Does air stop static electricity from building up?
faq.a: Air is a poor conductor, meaning it does not easily allow charge to flow away. This can help static charges build up to a high level.
asks: Does the air affect static charge?

facts: Static electricity is an imbalance of electric charge.
Friction can cause the transfer of electrons between materials.
Induction charges an object by bringing a charged object nearby.
A spark is a visible discharge of accumulated static charge.

quiz.say: Which method transfers charge by physical rubbing?
quiz.why: Friction directly involves rubbing two materials together to move electrons.

wrong.0: Induction requires the charged object to stay separate from the neutral object.
wrong.1: A spark is the result, not the method of charging itself.
wrong.2: Contact is a general term, but friction specifies the rubbing action.

quiz.say: If you bring a negative rod near a neutral ball, what happens first?

options.show: The rod loses all its charge
options.say: The rod loses all its charge

options.show: The ball becomes charged by induction
options.say: The ball becomes charged by induction

options.show: Nothing happens because they are not touching
options.say: Nothing happens because they are not touching

quiz.why: Bringing the rod near the ball causes the ball's charges to separate, giving it a charge.

wrong.0: The rod only influences the ball; it does not necessarily lose all its charge.
wrong.2: Repulsion only happens if the ball gains the same charge as the rod.
wrong.3: Induction works even without physical contact.

quiz.say: What is the visible jump of electricity from static buildup?
quiz.why: A spark is the visible sign that the built-up charge has jumped across a gap.

wrong.1: Induction is the process of charging, not the visible discharge.
wrong.2: Friction is the action, not the resulting visible jump.
wrong.3: Neutralization is the state after the charge has left, not the jump itself.
